contentEn:
If you are planning a renovation in Metro Vancouver, the first question on your mind is probably: "How much will this cost?" The honest answer depends on project type, scope, material choices, and your neighbourhood. Unlike most renovation websites that give you vague national averages, we share real prices from our own completed projects across Metro Vancouver.

This guide covers every major project type — kitchen, bathroom, basement, whole-house, cabinet refinishing, and commercial — with cost ranges backed by actual 聚星装修 project data from 2024–2026.

Kitchen Renovation Cost Vancouver 2026

Kitchen renovations are the most popular home improvement project in Metro Vancouver. Prices vary significantly by scope:

  • Basic refresh (new countertops, cabinet door refacing, hardware, paint): $14,000–$20,000
  • Mid-range (full cabinetry, quartz countertops, tile backsplash, lighting): $25,000–$35,000
  • Premium custom (waterfall island, premium appliances, custom cabinetry): $35,000–$72,000

Real examples from our portfolio:

  • Coquitlam condo kitchen: $25,000–$27,000
  • Langley townhouse white shaker cabinets and quartz: $20,000–$23,000
  • Langley kitchen with waterfall island: $28,000–$30,000
  • Burnaby custom wood-vein cabinets and gold fixtures: $35,000–$40,000
  • Vancouver full custom with premium finishes: $70,000–$72,000

Timeline: 3–6 weeks depending on scope and material lead times.

Read our detailed Kitchen Renovation Cost Guide →

Bathroom Renovation Cost Vancouver 2026

Bathroom renovation costs in Vancouver vary widely by size, fixtures, and scope:

  • Basic update (new vanity, fixtures, paint, minor tile): $12,000–$18,000
  • Standard renovation (full tile, new shower, vanity, glass): $18,000–$28,000
  • Premium renovation (heated floors, curbless shower, custom vanity): $28,000–$45,000
  • Luxury/multi-bath (spa-level, multiple baths): $40,000–$60,000+

Real examples from our portfolio:

  • Vancouver master bath: $14,000–$16,000
  • Coquitlam standard bath with shower conversion: $14,000–$17,000
  • Maple Ridge custom glass door bath: $18,000–$21,000
  • Richmond dual-bath renovation: $25,000–$28,000
  • Delta 3.5 bath renovation: $40,000–$43,000
  • West Vancouver one-to-two bath: $57,000–$60,000

Timeline: 2–4 weeks for a single bath, 4–8 weeks for multi-bath projects.

Read our detailed Bathroom Renovation Cost Guide →

Basement Renovation Cost Vancouver 2026

Basement renovations — especially suite conversions — are one of the best real estate investments in Metro Vancouver:

  • Basic renovation (rec room, bathroom, storage, no kitchen): $30,000–$45,000
  • Full suite (one bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, separate entrance): $40,000–$65,000
  • High-end suite (two bedrooms, full kitchen, laundry, premium finishes): $60,000–$85,000

ROI: A legal basement suite in Metro Vancouver can generate $1,400–$2,200/month in rental income — renovations can pay for themselves in 2–4 years.

Read our detailed Basement Renovation Cost Guide →

Whole-House Renovation Cost Vancouver 2026

Whole-house renovations in Vancouver vary enormously by size, age of home, and scope:

  • Cosmetic whole-house (paint, flooring, fixtures, kitchen and bathroom refresh): $80,000–$150,000
  • Moderate whole-house (two bathrooms, kitchen, flooring, some structural): $150,000–$300,000
  • Full gut and rebuild (all systems, structural, premium finishes): $300,000–$600,000+

Read our detailed Whole-House Renovation Cost Guide →

Cabinet Refinishing Cost Vancouver

Instead of full cabinet replacement, refinishing can give your kitchen a fresh look at a fraction of the cost:

  • Cabinet painting (professional spray paint): $3,000–$8,000
  • Cabinet door replacement (new doors, keep frames): $5,000–$15,000
  • Cabinet refacing (new veneer on frames, new doors): $10,000–$25,000

Commercial Renovation Cost Vancouver 2026

Commercial renovations in Metro Vancouver are priced per square foot:

  • Basic office refresh: $30–$60/sq ft
  • Standard office fit-out: $60–$120/sq ft
  • High-end commercial: $120–$200+/sq ft

Speak with our commercial team about your project →

How to Budget for Your Vancouver Renovation

Most homeowners allocate 10–20% below their maximum budget for contingencies. Older homes (pre-1980) should budget higher — structural issues and outdated electrical or plumbing are common discoveries.
